Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification outlining the anterior and inferior borders of the heart, specifically following the contour of the right ventricle and atrioventricular groove. This "eggshell" calcification pattern is pathognomonic for constrictive calcified pericarditis, which aligns with the clinical presentation of a systolic murmur potentially caused by extrinsic compression or associated valvular pathology.
